In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of vitamin-D metabolites with the hormonal-induced Ca2+-signaling pathway in osteoblastic UMR-106 cells.
the interaction of the two most important regulators of calcium homeostasis, parathyroid hormone and calcitriol, at the cellular level.
the interaction between vitamin D and other hormones in bone cells and the mechanisms by which vitamin D exerts its effects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
1,25-(OH)2D3 is an inhibitor of the PTH-induced Ca2+ signal transduction system, and that this inhibition occurs at the level of the inositol 4,5-bisphosphate pathway.
the effect of 1.25(OH) 2D3 in osteoblast like cells is to reduce the amount of calcium that is mobilised from the intracellular stores in response to PTH or PGE2.
1,25-(OH)2-D3 inhibits the PTH-induced increase in cytosolic free Ca2+ in UMR-106 osteoblast-like cell line by inhibiting the PTH-induced production of IP3.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
1,25D3 blunts the [Ca2+](i) transduction pathway of calciotropic hormones, and the effect is mediated by a selective action on hormonal-induced [Ca2+]-mobilization from intracellular stores.
1,25D3 blunts hormonal-elevated cytoplasmic free calcium in osteoblast cells.
the vitamin D metabolite 1,25 dihydroxyvitamin D3 inhibits the calcium signaling pathway in osteoblast cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
vitamin D metabolites can blunt the Ca2+ signaling pathway activated by parathyroid hormone and other bone-active hormones.
